Yes, I agree with the direction: the route should be much smaller than PR #344/#382 made it.

The important caveat is that “reuse implement with `base_branch=agent/rubrics`” is conceptually right, but not literally safe with the current workflow. `agent-implement.yml` supports `base_branch` and `implementation_prompt` already: [`agent-implement.yml#L26-L40`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-implement.yml#L26-L40), and the dispatch helper already forwards those inputs: [`.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-implement.ts#L17-L39`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-implement.ts#L17-L39). But the workflow then checks out the implementation branch from `BASE_BRANCH` before running the local action: [`agent-implement.yml#L195-L226`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-implement.yml#L195-L226). If `BASE_BRANCH=agent/rubrics`, the workspace likely no longer has `.github/actions/run-agent-task` or `.agent/dist`, because `agent/rubrics` is a data branch. That is why the earlier PRs grew: they tried to preserve runtime-code trust boundaries, proposal PR behavior, direct-write modes, validation, and failure summaries all at once.

I would simplify the next version to **proposal-only**:

1. Add `add-rubrics` to route catalogs:
   - [`.agent/src/triage.ts#L12-L20`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/triage.ts#L12-L20)
   - [`.agent/src/triage.ts#L32`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/triage.ts#L32)
   - [`.agent/src/envelope.ts#L55-L71`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/envelope.ts#L55-L71)
   - [`.agent/src/run.ts#L125-L141`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L125-L141)

2. Add `.github/prompts/agent-add-rubrics.md`.

3. Route `/add-rubrics` through the existing implementation-like router path, but with:
   - `IMPLEMENTATION_ROUTE=add-rubrics`
   - `IMPLEMENTATION_PROMPT=agent-add-rubrics`
   - `BASE_BRANCH=agent/rubrics`

4. Make the implementation workflow keep Sepo runtime from the default branch while editing the `agent/rubrics` branch. This is the one mechanical change needed to make your idea work cleanly.

5. Open a normal PR targeting `agent/rubrics`. Do not implement direct commit mode in this pass.

6. Add focused tests for route parsing, envelope validation, prompt selection, and the dispatch inputs.

So yes: the mental model should be “implement route, different prompt, rubrics branch as the PR base.” The only adjustment is preserving the default-branch runtime while the editable worktree is based on `agent/rubrics`. I’d start from that narrow plan and leave direct commits, extra mode inference, and complex summary handling out of scope unless explicitly requested.
